items.title: Fonepay, Nabil Bank launch digital payment app for foreign visitors
items.summary: Fonepay and Nabil Bank have launched a digital payment app for foreign visitors in Nepal. The item is headline only.
items.idea: We could offer a visitor mode in the Birbank app for foreign tourists in Azerbaijan, with QR payments funded by a card that needs no local account, starting with the Bir Pay QR flow.

dependencies: CBA rules on non-resident users and foreign-card onboarding
Acquirer or payment scheme support for foreign cards on Bir Pay QR
Merchant acceptance agreements with tourist-heavy venues
risks: Fraud risk from foreign cards with no local identity check
Foreign card FX costs may reduce usage
sim.pilot: Run a two-month pilot with one cluster of Baku hotels and restaurants, limited to foreign cards and Bir Pay QR.
sim.mechanism: A visitor mode in the Birbank app lets foreign tourists pay by Bir Pay QR using a foreign card with no local account, while the existing QR payment flow stays unchanged.
sim.segment: Foreign visitors to Azerbaijan with international cards and no local account

items.title: Kazakhstan plans geolocation tracking for microloan applications to curb fraud
items.summary: Kazakhstan's financial regulator ARDFM requires microfinance organisations to collect geolocation during mobile app transactions and loan applications, block issuance on remote-controlled or rooted devices, and send alerts on logins and password or phone changes. Anti-spoofing liveness checks and integration with the National Bank's Anti-Fraud Center are also required.
items.idea: We could add login and phone-change alerts plus a root or remote-control check before card-to-card and phone-number transfers, starting with the transfer flow in the app.

dependencies: CBA requirements on authentication and fraud controls in digital channels
Kapital fraud and risk team sign-off on rules
risks: False positives may block legitimate users on custom Android builds
Device data collection raises privacy and data residency questions
sim.pilot: Run four weeks of shadow-mode root and remote-control detection on the transfer flow, logging only and not blocking.
sim.mechanism: Before card-to-card and phone-number transfers, the app checks for rooted or remote-controlled devices, sends alerts on new logins and phone-number changes, and blocks high-risk transfers until the user confirms.
sim.segment: Retail users making card-to-card and phone-number transfers, mainly on Android

items.title: Central Bank of Egypt launches card tokenisation on Android devices
items.summary: The Central Bank of Egypt has launched card tokenisation on Android devices. The item is a headline only.
items.idea: We could check whether our Android wallet flow supports token-based card storage and, if not, scope tokenisation for Android card add-to-wallet.

dependencies: Card scheme token service provider certification
CBA rules on tokenisation, which are not yet confirmed in our context
Android host card emulation wallet SDK
risks: May overlap with existing wallet features and cannibalise them
Egyptian rules may not transfer to Azerbaijan
sim.pilot: Spend two weeks auditing the current Android add-to-wallet flow and confirming whether token-based storage is supported.
sim.mechanism: Android users can add their Birbank cards to a phone wallet as device-bound tokens, so the card number is not stored on the device; this would extend the existing wallet flow if Android is not yet covered.
sim.segment: Android users who want to pay in-store and in apps with their phone

items.title: Klarna rolls out One-Time virtual card in Canada
items.summary: Klarna has rolled out a One-Time virtual card in Canada. The item is a headline only, so details are limited.
items.idea: We could add a single-use virtual card issued in the app for online checkout, starting with a pilot for one-off merchant payments.

dependencies: Card scheme virtual card issuance and BIN setup
CBA rules on virtual card issuance, not yet confirmed in our context
risks: Click to Pay and Apple Pay may already cover most secure online checkout needs
Single-use cards may confuse users and cause failed payments
Fraud rules need tuning for one-time card patterns
sim.pilot: Issue one-time cards to a 200-user beta for one merchant category, such as travel or digital goods.
sim.mechanism: The user creates a single-use virtual card in the Birbank app for one online checkout; the card number expires after one payment and cannot be reused.
sim.segment: Online shoppers who want to limit exposure on one-off merchant payments
